law: laws/BOHEMIA_THE_PIXEL_BIBLE.md — M17 (one master palette, families are subsets) and M18 (value skeleton first, hue last)
supersedes_for_design: records/target/BOHEMIA_MASTER_PALETTE.json, which is a QUANTIZATION of the target screen, not a designed palette
method: PASS 1 designed the value skeleton in grey with every band and separation decided on purpose. PASS 2 put hue on it, each family taking its hue from the approved corpus so the colour stays Paolo's.

ground.why: the biggest surface and the one nobody should look at (M2). Mean ~104, which is where the approved corpus already sits — this band is NOT being redesigned, it is being kept.

structure.why: building faces. Mean ~139, again where the approved corpus sits. Clears ground by 35 points.

top.why: roofs and sky-facing planes. Mean ~78 — the ONE band that moves, DOWN from the corpus 110.2, because at 110 a terracotta roof sat 6.5 points off the gravel yard and vanished in greyscale (M14). Fired clay is a dark red material; making it lighter than a stucco wall was my error, not the corpus's.

accent.why: the reserved slots content needs: dead-dark glass and door interiors at the bottom, paint and sun-caught ridge at the top. Deliberately spans the whole range because accents are exactly the things that must escape their band.

dead_glass.why: act-1 dead dark glass and door interiors — the one thing that must sit BELOW every ground step

shadow_core.why: the darkest thing in the world, still not black

paint.why: road and stall paint, chalked, never pure white

sun_caught.why: the ridge course and anything the sun hits square — the only slot allowed near the ceiling

NOT_APPROVED: designed, gated, and NOT judged. Paolo has not seen it. It is the blocker in front of the eighteen tile forms, not a verdict.
